newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe wants Mitterrand wiretaps review.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe wants Mitterrand wiretaps review.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, under pressure to lift official secrecy over illegal wiretaps under late president Francois Mitterrand, ordered a review on Tuesday of new evidence found by the security services.

Juppe's office said he had decided to have qualified experts on security intercepts study files belonging to the head of Mitterrand's rogue anti-terror unit, which were discovered in February in a garage outside Paris.
"Out of concern for procedural legality, the prime minister has decided to have these documents examined by qualified experts," his office said in a statement.

Once the National Control Commission on Security Intercepts had given its opinion on the findings, "the prime minister will ask that all the documents on wiretaps which were not carried out by the interministerial communications group be handed over to the investigating magistrate without delay".
No one could use "defence secrecy" to withhold any document which was not strictly legal, the statement said.

The announcement appeared to clear the way for the judge probing illegal wiretapping between 1982 and 1986 to have access to files on many of the estimated 2,000 targets bugged by Mitterrand's anti-terror unit, including lawyers, politicians, journalists and actors.
